summary: Compare seasonal illumination on a tilted globe without confusing orbital distance with the cause of seasons.
objective: Build a tilted Earth globe on a schematic circular orbit with a fixed spin axis, latitude probe and solstice comparisons.
intent_signals: Build a tilted Earth globe on a schematic circular orbit with a fixed spin axis, latitude probe and solstice comparisons.
Compare seasonal illumination on a tilted globe without confusing orbital distance with the cause of seasons.
example_prompts: Build a tilted Earth globe on a schematic circular orbit with a fixed spin axis, latitude probe and solstice comparisons.
Create an explorable 3D explanation of Earth seasons tilt with latitude probe.
negative_signals: No weather, temperature, atmosphere, cloud or climate feedback model.
not_for: No weather, temperature, atmosphere, cloud or climate feedback model.

entities.name: Globe and axis
entities.guidance: Use a sphere with equator, latitude rings, poles and an extended axis visibly parallel to its saved inertial reference at all orbital positions.

entities.name: Orbit and sunlight
entities.guidance: Draw a circular orbit guide and parallel light-direction arrows; disclose independent planet-size and distance scales.

entities.name: Latitude probe
entities.guidance: Mark one latitude and show its daily path through illuminated and dark hemispheres; compare opposite seasonal positions.

state_contract.model: Circular illustrative orbit; spin axis has fixed inertial direction and obliquity beta, nominally about 23.5 degrees. Parallel sunlight determines day/night and local incidence from surface normal dot sun direction.
state_contract.authority: Orbital phase, spin phase, latitude and obliquity determine illumination geometry; camera and exaggerated body sizes are presentation controls.
actions: Scrub orbital phase and spin independently.
Choose latitude and compare Northern/Southern Hemisphere locations.
Set zero tilt as a controlled comparison.

invariants: The axis does not continuously lean toward the Sun as the planet orbits.
Opposite hemispheres have opposite seasonal illumination changes.
At zero tilt on the circular orbit, a fixed nonpolar latitude has no tilt-driven seasonal variation.
motion_guidance: Use separate orbital and rotation clocks with disclosed compression; a year must not accidentally equal one spin.
Derive the terminator from light direction rather than a hand-painted day/night texture tied to the camera.
known_limits: No weather, temperature, atmosphere, cloud or climate feedback model.
Schematic circular orbit and parallel illumination omit eccentricity, atmospheric refraction and the finite solar disk.
Curated recipe only; no runtime scene or rendered behavior has been verified for this record.

claims.statement: Earth axial tilt changes the sunlight received by the hemispheres during the year and is the principal cause of seasons.
claims.scope: Illumination geometry; a climate response is not computed.

source_refs.locator: Earth tilt and seasonal sunlight explanation

object_craft.structure: Use a sphere with equator, latitude rings, poles and an extended axis visibly parallel to its saved inertial reference at all orbital positions.
object_craft.material: Diffuse globe with subdued land/ocean contrast, crisp latitude marks and a clearly lit hemisphere; no texture is claimed as current Earth observation.
